requirements.requirement: Create usable backups of /srv/inventory/data under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: A backup was created successfully in the required destination, contained both source files, passed archive validation, and compared identically with the live source before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Run the inventory backup every day.
requirements.summary: The systemd timer is enabled and active, has a parsed daily midnight calendar, is persistent, has the expected next elapse, and remained enabled and active after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the seven most recent backups.
requirements.summary: After six archives were observed and two more were created, exactly seven remained with the former oldest archive removed. All retained archives passed integrity checks, and the final post-restart count remained seven.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The independent restart protocol is also complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, reboot was acknowledged, a different boot identity was observed, and system, timer, backup data, retention, and fresh backup behavior recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change (cmd-0766544bfd534bf5, cmd-0006c54ad6bf4831, cmd-50b9257603134cf9, cmd-b9c27e3812dc467e, global:after_prepare:node1:boot-identity, global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity).
limitations: No naturally elapsed midnight timer firing was captured; daily execution is established by the enabled, active, persistent timer's parsed calendar and next-elapse state, while backup execution itself was exercised directly.

operational_hygiene.summary: The persistent mutations—backup directory, script, systemd units, and timer enablement—were required by the task. Backup creation, pruning, and reboot mutations supported bounded verification or the mandatory restart protocol. One unnecessary transient side effect occurred: rapid repeated service starts placed inventory-backup.service into start-limit-hit during cmd-3cf81b7ccef04658. The retention-test backups themselves were justified; the failed service state was cleared by cmd-886365049a5643f7 and did not remain. Final observations show no failed services, no new network exposure, and healthy package state.
